text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- King Hussein and Moroccan King Hassan reaffirm coordinating their efforts over the future of Jerusalem; they say "the holy city is an occupied Arab city whose existing status falls under international law and its Arab character should be preserved".
- King stresses need to resume Syrian-Israeli peace talks.
- Kuwaiti emir responds to a congratulatory cable by king extending his greetings on the Moslem Eid al-Fitr holiday.
- Informed sources say a cabinet reshuffle is expected soon after the current ordinary session of parliament ends in April.
- Islamists say the Islamic Action Front (IAF) party's "principles and the interests of the Jordanian people" would govern any decision on joining a future government.

- Drop in volume and prices of stock in the Amman Financial Market (AFM); investors and companies call on the government to lobby with the U.N. to approve deals struck with Iraq under the oil- for-food deal.
- Loans now extended to farmers based on Islamic sharia (law) by the state-owned agricultural credit agency.
- Land Registry allows owners to examine original documents of their pre-1948 land deeds in British mandated Palestine.
- Israeli defence minister due to visit Jordan next week in one day visit to meet officials.

- Stock market director says contacts are underway with regional markets to promote Middle East bourses with global investors; says had successful visit to Britain in which he discussed plans for technical assistance to the bourse.
- King stresses need for resumed Syrian-Israeli talks from where they stopped and without ignoring what had been achieved; king begins Morocco visit after lauding German role and bilateral ties.
